aspects.says: the one-period selection model: one 0-1 variable per project, a budget row, must-do, parent and alternative rows
aspects.reason: the model every later example branches on; it was taught in lesson 1.1.3, and the practices use their own models

aspects.says: the LP relaxation keeps every row and lets each 0-1 variable range over [0, 1], so its value bounds every plan from above
basis: section:Dropping Integrality Gives an LP Whose Value Bounds Every Plan From Above
aspects.reason: a proof read on the page; the quiz asks what the bound rules out

aspects.says: a variable is fractional when its LP value is more than a tolerance away from the nearest whole number
basis: section:A Fractional Value Marks the Variable to Branch On

aspects.says: branching puts every integer plan in exactly one child and the fractional LP point in neither
basis: section:Branching Splits the Problem Into Two Children That Keep Every Integer Plan

aspects.says: a child is the parent's LP with one bound changed, and its LP value is never above the parent's
basis: section:Each Child Is the Same LP With One Bound Changed

aspects.says: a general integer at a fractional value v splits into x <= floor(v) and x >= ceil(v)
basis: section:A General Integer Branches on Floor and Ceiling

aspects.says: a node whose LP is infeasible or integral is a leaf, and an integral LP solution is the best plan in its node
basis: section:Branching Stops at a Node Whose LP Is Infeasible or Integral
aspects.reason: read from the printed tree; lesson 3.2.2's practice classifies nodes, and the quiz asks about an integral node

aspects.says: what an LP relaxation's value says about a reported plan
basis: section:Dropping Integrality Gives an LP Whose Value Bounds Every Plan From Above

aspects.says: the children of a general integer variable
basis: section:A General Integer Branches on Floor and Ceiling

aspects.says: what the search does at a node with a whole-number LP solution
